title: Audit sequence-id rollover caused missing entries — reconciliation and prevention
creator: Maya Chen
description: During a routine certificate/KMS epoch rotation on 2025-03-01 we observed a class of audit events missing from the central compliance trail. The audit-forwarder assigns monotonically increasing sequence_ids per source; under a rare combination of sequence counter wrap (32-bit counter used by a legacy forwarder) and batch reorder during high SSO load, newer events were ingested with lower sequence_ids and the reconciliation dedupe logic considered earlier-seen higher sequence_ids as duplicates and discarded them. This ticket tracks the reconciliation, hot fixes, and longer-term prevention work.
impact: Internal compliance trail gaps for ~2.3k events spanning ~25 minutes across three customer tenants. No plaintext payloads were lost (events were held in local forwarder buffer), but the central audit index omitted entries which affected compliance exports and delayed internal investigations. Customer-facing systems (API auth) were not functionally degraded; primary impact is on audit completeness and downstream export deliveries.

root_cause: A legacy audit-forwarder process used a 32-bit sequence counter that wrapped after high-volume bursts and during restart windows. The central reconciliation/dedup logic assumed strictly monotonic sequence_ids per source and used sequence comparison to drop duplicates; wrapped sequence_ids violated this invariant. The wrap coincided with certificate reloads that temporarily changed source identifiers and with an SSO traffic spike that increased batching and reordering probability.
mitigation:
Immediate: adjusted reconcilier to fallback to timestamp+unique-id comparison when sequence discontinuities are detected and added an alert for non-monotonic windows. Hotfix completed and deployed to all regions (runtime-1.22 patch).
Short-term: enforce 64-bit sequence counters in forwarders, revert legacy forwarder binaries where possible, and add post-restart buffer draining latency to reduce reordering.
Long-term: replace sequence-based dedupe with an idempotent delivery scheme (idempotency-key + ingestion-ack) and add integration tests that simulate wrap/restart under load.
